question: Phosphorus is an essential input for agricultural food production. At the same time, the EU is heavily dependent on phosphorus imports from a few third countries, with Russia being one of the largest suppliers. Despite Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine, in 2025 the EU imported phosphorus products from Russia worth almost EUR 900 million. The value of imports since February 2022 is around EUR 3.5 billion.

The EU’s own rules are making domestic production more difficult. This is both geopolitically irresponsible and politically inconsistent. There is technology available that makes it possible to extract high-quality phosphorus from incinerated sewage sludge, and the recovered product has already been approved for organic fertilisers. Despite this, however, Regulation (EC) No 767/2009 prohibits its use in animal feed.
With the above in mind: 1.
Does the Commission intend to review the exemption in Regulation (EC) No 767/2009 to allow for the safe recovery of nutrients from manure and sewage sludge?
What specific action is the Commission taking to reduce the EU’s dependence on imports of phosphorus, and how will this be reflected in the forthcoming Circular Economy Act?
Does the Commission intend to bring forward proposals to phase out imports of phosphorus products from Russia along the lines of the phasing-out of Russian oil?
